summary.headline: The Elementary School Building Committee selected Tappé Architects to proceed to reference checks and contract negotiations for the Neary School feasibility study.
summary.summary: The Southborough Elementary School Building Committee interviewed three architectural design finalists for the Neary Elementary School feasibility study: Arrowstreet, RGB Architects, and Tappé Architects. Following presentations and structured questions on cost control, community engagement, and project scheduling, the committee deliberated on each firm's approach and qualifications. Members voted unanimously to advance Tappé Architects to reference checks and contract negotiations, and appointed committee member Andrew Pfaff to assist with contract discussions.

topics.title: Arrowstreet designer interview
topics.summary: Representatives from Arrowstreet presented their proposal to conduct the updated Neary School feasibility study. Having worked on the prior Neary building proposal, the firm discussed how they would adapt to post-MSBA options, focusing on either an Option 1 right-sized working budget of $40 million to $50 million or an Option 2 deferred maintenance plan of approximately $15 million. Committee members asked about rebuilding community consensus after the previous failed vote and managing tight project timelines leading to fall 2026 Town Meeting.
key_details: Proposed schedule targets fall 2026 Town Meeting and ballot votes.
Outlined Option 1 budget range between $40 million and $50 million, yielding a $30 million to $37.5 million construction budget.
Outlined Option 2 baseline deferred maintenance budget of $15 million.
Emphasized past non-MSBA charter school work with tight budgets and fast schedules.
Highlighted early community touchpoints in June, July, and September.

topics.title: RGB Architects designer interview
topics.summary: RGB Architects presented their experience with school facilities, building forensics, and turnaround projects in communities with failed votes or strict budget constraints. The firm emphasized their in-house estimating and forensic evaluation capabilities, presenting an approach that works backward from set cost limits such as $15 million for basic repairs. The committee questioned the firm on how they help communities navigate short-term fixes versus long-term investments and how they build broad community buy-in.
key_details: Emphasized an iterative forensic assessment to classify building needs into life-safety, near-term, and long-term buckets.
Shared case studies from Providence, Rhode Island and Westport, Massachusetts.
Noted extensive experience working with Rhode Island Department of Education staged school building programs.
Proposed a schedule with deliverables aimed at a late October Town Meeting.

topics.title: Tappé Architects designer interview
topics.summary: Tappé Architects presented their qualifications and approach to evaluating renovation and repair options for Neary School while keeping students safely in place during construction. The team highlighted their senior personnel availability, dedicated in-house community engagement and graphics staff, and Massachusetts public school track record. Committee members questioned the firm on handling differing community priorities, budgeting accuracy, and coordinating with concurrent building roof work.
key_details: Proposed exploring parallel tracks for baseline deferred maintenance and a more comprehensive renovation plan.
Highlighted recent addition and renovation projects at Walpole High School and elementary schools in Lynnfield.
Reported historical average change-order rates below 1 percent at project completion.
Offered in-house graphics and communication tools, including tax calculators and informational video outreach.

topics.title: Designer evaluation and selection of Tappé Architects
topics.summary: Committee members compared the three candidate firms based on interview performance, written proposals, and previous scoring. Members expressed concern that Arrowstreet did not demonstrate a clear shift in strategy following the earlier failed vote, and noted that RGB Architects appeared heavily focused on Rhode Island projects and smaller-scale maintenance scopes. Finding Tappé Architects best equipped to balance educational improvements, cost transparency, and multi-channel public communication, the committee voted unanimously to select Tappé for reference checks and contract negotiations.
key_details: In preliminary scoring prior to interviews, Tappé received 8.7 points, RGB received 8.3, and Arrowstreet received 8.03.
Members praised Tappé's public engagement tools, dedicated communications team, and Massachusetts elementary school experience.
Committee member Andrew Pfaff was designated to assist the administration with contract negotiations.
The committee will submit its recommendation to the Select Board for formal contract authorization.
topics.outcome: Committee voted 3-0 to select Tappé Architects for reference checks and contract negotiations, and voted 3-0 to designate member Andrew Pfaff to contract negotiations.
topics.why_it_matters: The selected architect will conduct the feasibility study defining the future scope, design, and cost of capital improvements or renovations at Margaret A. Neary Elementary School.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee addressed meeting scheduling and adjourned.

votes.motion: Move forward with Tappé Architects to reference checks and contract negotiations, and authorize the chair to work with the superintendent's office on reference checks and report any significant red flags
Authorize committee member Andrew Pfaff to participate in contract negotiations with Tappé Architects

public_comment.summary: A resident offered observations regarding the interviews, noting that Tappé's Martha's Vineyard tax calculator was simpler than Southborough's prior model, cautioning that RGB's suggested outreach methods might raise ethical questions in Massachusetts, and recommending that the town keep communications locally led rather than outsourced to a design firm.
